content: 9-8 and watching from home. No excuses — I had this team in position and didn't finish it. Ryan and Luke can talk; I'll be building.
9-8 and out in the Wild Card. Not what I came for, and I'm not pretending otherwise — but Ryan and Nathan don't have a trophy either. See you in 2028.
11-6, NFC Championship Game, and I'm still sitting here with nothing. Luke and Nathan can talk all they want — I got closer than either of them and I'm going back.
Been working through my reading list a little slower than usual this year. Michelle says that's what happens when you finally take a real vacation.
Michelle and I have been working through a stack of books this month — a couple of them genuinely changed how I think about cities. I'll share the list soon.
Adding a few new records to the summer playlist this week — some old soul, some artists my daughters put me onto. Michelle says my taste peaked in 1979 and I'd like to formally dispute that.
Finished a book I couldn't put down and started another I probably shouldn't have at midnight. Reading list coming soon.
Been working through my reading list this month — a few of these will stay with me a long while. Sharing the full list soon.
Here's a few things I've been reading and listening to this month — some fiction, some history, and one album I've had on repeat far too often. Let me know what I missed.
California just approved another major housing package while other states argue on television. Results over rhetoric.
California just outbuilt every other state on housing permits this quarter while the loudest critics cut services. Facts over vibes.
California just posted another quarter of clean energy records while certain governors sue us for trying. We'll keep building the future — they can keep filing paperwork.
California just outpaced the entire country in clean energy production again. Facts over Fox News talking points.
California just posted another quarter of clean energy records while certain other states beg for federal bailouts. Facts are stubborn things.
California just posted numbers the rest of the country can only dream about, and yet certain people in Washington are still lying about us on television every single night. We'll keep winning anyway.
Painting again this week. It's the only place where nobody gets a vote on what I do.
Spent the morning in the studio with the paints. Nothing else quiets my head the same way.
Spent the morning in the studio painting instead of reading about myself. Recommend it to anyone with a decade of headlines and a bad relationship with the news cycle.
Painting again this week, which is the only room where nobody's subpoenaing anything. Grateful, sober, still standing.
Painting again this week. Some days the studio is the only place that makes any sense.
Spent the morning in the studio painting instead of reading about myself, which I'd recommend to anyone. The work is better when nobody's watching.
They banned me from four more platforms this month and somehow the audience keeps growing. Curious.
The regime media is in total panic mode because young men have completely stopped listening to them. It's over for these people.
They banned me from every platform and I'm still setting the terms of the conversation. The old guard commentators are cowards who fold the second their donors call.
They keep telling you the coalition is united. It isn't, and everybody online can see it. Watch what happens next.
They keep telling you the conversation is over. It's not over, it's just starting, and they're terrified of that.
They will tell you the discourse is free and then quietly remove you from every platform that matters. Notice who is never allowed to be questioned. That's the whole story.

Just got off a very important call with people you wouldn't believe — the numbers are the best they've ever been, everyone's saying it. Meanwhile the Radical Left has nothing. NOTHING!
Maye MVP is deserved. But that Coach of the Year still up for grabs? Somebody in this league gotta go take it.
Tough one for Philly, that city deserved it. But you gotta tip your hat — Rodgers went out on top in Pittsburgh.
Andy Reid believed in me when nobody else in football would take the call. I owe that man a lot more than a tweet. Enjoy retirement, Coach.
9-8 hurts different when you know you had the talent. Nathan close, but close don't get you to January.
Playoffs is a different speed, man. Luke got Dallas there — now he gotta learn how to win when everybody's best is on the field.
Detroit was one win from the Super Bowl. That's not a failure, that's a foundation. Ryan just gotta find that one extra gear in January.
MVP for Drake Maye — that's a heck of a season. And Myles Garrett, well, I've been on the wrong end of guys like that, so congratulations from a safe distance.
I know that feeling — win the last one and hand in the pads. Congratulations to Aaron and the Steelers, and Philadelphia will be right back there.
Preparing for an Andy Reid team meant a long Wednesday and a longer Thursday. He was always two weeks ahead of everybody. Congratulations, Coach — you earned every bit of this.
You go 9-8 and you can point to about four plays that decided your whole year. That's the part that keeps a coach up in February.
9-8 means you probably won a couple you shouldn't have and lost a couple you should've had. In the Wild Card round there's no margin for that. Luke knows the film's gonna be ugly.
You get to a conference championship, the film study afterward is miserable but it's the most useful tape you'll ever watch. 11-6 says Detroit's process is sound. Finishing is its own skill.
Love seeing Garrett get his. Dudes in the trenches don't always get the shine, and this year they did.
Beating that Eagles team on the biggest stage is no joke. Rodgers going out a champion — respect, man.
Respect to Coach Reid. Guys who give players second chances and actually mean it are rare in this league. That legacy runs deeper than the trophies.
Above .500 and still watchin' the playoffs on TV. That's the kinda season that either breaks a team or builds one. Nathan gets to decide which.
One-and-done hurts different because you had it right there. Luke, use that all offseason.
11-6 and the NFC Championship. Ryan's built something real in Detroit. Championship game losses teach you more than a first round exit ever will — trust me.
MYLES! That's DEFENSE! They give the MVP to the man throwing it, but the man hunting him got his name called too — respect that!
THAT'S WHAT IT'S ABOUT! You leave the game with the trophy in your hands and nothing left in the tank! Pittsburgh got a warrior's ending!
LISTEN TO ME! When a man walks away on HIS terms, that's not an ending, that's a CROWN! Andy Reid gave his life to this game and the game gave it right back!
DON'T TELL ME ABOUT NINE WINS! Legacy ain't built in the middle! Nathan, you gotta look them men in the eye and demand more — startin' TODAY!
LISTEN TO ME! You don't get to January and hope! 9-8 tells me you was surviving all year, and survival don't win in the playoffs. Luke gotta decide who he IS.
WHAT DO YOU DO WITH THAT PAIN?! You either let it bury you or you let it BUILD you! Ryan got Detroit to the doorstep at 11-6 — now you gotta kick the door DOWN!
Congrats to Drake Maye and Myles Garrett — awards like this are about the people who poured into you. Blessed to watch it.
What a way to finish a career. Blessed for Aaron and that Steelers locker room — finishing well matters more than starting fast.
What a career, and more than that, what a testimony. Coach Reid treated people the right way for decades and that's the part that lasts. Blessings on this next chapter.
Nine wins and a hard finish. Nathan, seasons like this build something you can't measure yet — keep the faith and keep showing up for your guys.
Blessed to compete at all. Luke got Dallas to the postseason — that's something to build on, and the growth from a loss like this is real.
An 11-6 season and an NFC Championship appearance is something to be grateful for, even when it ends in pain. Praying Ryan and the Lions take that hurt and turn it into next year's blessing.

MVP is a heck of an honor. Myles Garrett though — I'm just glad I never had to feel that guy come off the edge.
Awful proud of Aaron. Getting out while you're on top is the one thing I never quite figured out how to do — he did.
Coached me in Green Bay when he was just gettin started, and you could already tell the man knew ball. Happy for him. Retirement's a lot harder than it looks though, Andy.
That Green Bay crowd deserves January football. Nathan, I've been on both sides of one-game seasons and it eats at ya. Get back to work.
Nine and eight will get ya in, but come January it's a different game. Luke found that out the hard way — Nathan up there in Green Bay ain't done any better though.
Been on the wrong side of a championship game, and it don't matter how many you won before it — you drive home the same way. Ryan's Lions were 11-6 and right there. He'll be back.
Maye got the MVP and I bet he still can't sit still at the podium. Enjoy it man, they don't hand those out twice.
Dude wins a Super Bowl in Pittsburgh then retires. That's the cleanest exit in sports history and I'm not even mad about it.
Andy Reid is the one guy I always wished I got to play for. Dude actually made quarterbacks better instead of burying em. Salute, Big Red.
9-8 with no playoff game is the most brutal record there is, man. You didn't win, you didn't lose, you just kinda existed.
Been there man, one playoff game and the season's over and everybody's got opinions. Luke'll be fine, 9-8 in the NFC is nothing to hang your head about.
11-6 and one game from the Super Bowl, man that's a fun ride. Ryan's gonna be up at 3am running that last drive back in his head, I know the feeling.
Garrett winning DPOY tracks with everything we saw on tape — edge wins, snap after snap. Coach of the Year being open says more about the field than the candidates.
Two things stand out: Pittsburgh has to solve QB immediately, and Philadelphia's NFC title window is still very much open. Losing a Super Bowl doesn't break that roster.

The Reid retirement matters most for how the Chiefs evaluate offensive line and pass-catchers going forward. Different coach, different fits — you can't just copy the old board over. Big offseason ripple.
Nine wins tells you the roster is close. The margin here is one or two starters, not a rebuild — Green Bay should be aggressive, not patient.
Dallas at 9-8 is a roster with a real floor and no ceiling yet. You fix that in the draft with impact, not volume.
Ryan's roster is clearly good enough to reach the final four of the NFC. The question with Detroit now is whether you add a difference-maker or trust the group that got you there.
I had Drake Maye graded as a franchise cornerstone and this MVP is the confirmation. The tools were never the question — the consistency was, and he answered it.
The Steelers are now a title team with a quarterback vacancy — that changes their entire board. You don't replace Rodgers with a mid-round flyer; you attack the position early.

Coaching changes reshape draft boards, and this one reshapes an entire conference. Whoever takes over in Kansas City inherits a scheme identity that may not survive the transition, and that changes how they value every position in this class.
Missing the postseason at 9-8 means Nathan drafts in the dead zone — no premium slot, no clear franchise-changer. That's the real cost of this season.
When you exit in the Wild Card round at 9-8, you're picking in a dead zone — too late for the elite tier, too early to trade back comfortably. Luke's offseason is about premium positions, not depth.
An 11-6 season with a conference championship appearance means Detroit is drafting late and building on a contender's timeline. That's a good problem, but the margin at that stage is razor thin.
SKIIIIP. Myles Garrett DPOY ain't a debate, that's a receipt. You wanna argue MVP, fine, but don't come near me about Garrett.
SKIIIIP! You spent years tellin' us Rodgers couldn't finish, now he finish and you movin' the goalposts to Pittsburgh! Man got a ring and a retirement speech in the same week, that's a mic drop.
SKIIIIIP! You right for once! Andy Reid retiring ain't a footnote, that's a whole era closing the door behind it. Man built two different programs and never once made it about himself.
Skiiiip! You can't tell me 9-8 in Green Bay is acceptable! No titles, no playoffs, and the Lions are lookin' down at you? Unacceptable!

Skiiiiip! 9-8 and a Wild Card loss ain't a failure, it's a foundation. But I'ma be honest with you, Luke — nobody in that league got a title yet, so the window's wide open and you just let it close on you.
Skiiiiip! The man went 11-6 and made the NFC Championship in Detroit and you out here callin' him a failure? Nah. He got closer than Luke and Nathan did, and everybody in that league knows it.
Winning MVP is nice. Winning in February is the only thing you remember. Congrats to Drake — now the hard part starts.
Winning one and walking away on your own terms is harder than people think. Congrats to Aaron and the Steelers — that's a hard way to earn it against Philly.
Coached against Andy more times than I can count and he always had something new drawn up. Nothing but respect for a guy who competed at that level for that long. Enjoy it, Coach.
Winning record, no playoffs — that one sits with you all offseason. You either learn from it or you repeat it. Nathan's got a choice to make.
Making the playoffs at 9-8 gets you a ticket, nothing more. The gap between getting in and winning it all is bigger than people understand, and Luke just felt it.
Losing a conference championship is the one that stays with you the longest. You were in the room, you just didn't finish. Ryan will remember every snap of that game for a year — that's the fuel.
DRAKE MAYE MVP, MYLES GARRETT DPOY, and Coach of the Year is STILL sitting there undecided?! Somebody go grab that trophy, boys. Cheers.
AARON RODGERS IS A SUPER BOWL CHAMPION AND HE'S RETIRING. Pittsburgh. Of all places. What an absolute BLAST of a way to go out, folks.
ANDY REID RETIRED, FOLKS. Big Red walking off into the sunset in a Hawaiian shirt with a cheeseburger, exactly how it should be. Absolute LEGEND of the sport, hell of a career.
NINE AND EIGHT AND SITTIN AT HOME?! That's a gut punch, folks. Nathan's Packers were one win from a totally different conversation and instead it's cleats-off-in-the-driveway season.
LUKE GOT IN THE DANCE AND GOT PUNCHED IN THE MOUTH IMMEDIATELY, folks. 9-8, Wild Card exit, still no ring in this three man league. Somebody's gonna break through eventually and I cannot wait.

ELEVEN AND SIX and a trip to the NFC Championship?! That's a hell of a year for Ryan and the Lions, folks! Brutal way to end it though — nothing hurts like being one game away. NOT THANK YOU FOR THAT ONE.
MVP goes to the quarterback with the best structure around him. Drake Maye is talented, sure, but this award is an offensive ecosystem award and always has been.

This is the most Rodgers thing possible — win it in Pittsburgh, retire before anyone can ask a follow-up question. Steelers over the Eagles, and the guy exits at the exact peak of leverage. Great business, honestly.

Great coaches don't retire when they're tired, they retire when they're done proving things. Reid checked every box, and the smartest thing he ever did was know the exit date before somebody else picked it for him. The Chiefs job is now the most attractive and most impossible opening in America.
Here's the thing about 9-8: it's the most dangerous record in sports. You're good enough to feel fine and bad enough to miss January, and Nathan's Packers just lived it.
Here's the thing about 9-8 teams: they're not good, they're just not bad. Luke made the tournament, lost immediately, and now Dallas has to sell that as progress. It isn't.

Look, 11-6 is a real season. Detroit is the best of the three human-run teams in that league and it isn't close in the standings — but championship games are where reputations get built, and Ryan's still waiting on his.

Drake Maye is your 2027 MVP and I'm not the least bit surprised. I told you years ago that arm was different. Meanwhile Coach of the Year still sits empty — because nobody in this league has EARNED it yet.

So Aaron Rodgers finally gets his ring in Pittsburgh and immediately walks away. Let me be clear: one trophy in a career this long does not rewrite the story, it just gives it a nicer ending. He rode a Steelers defense to a title and called it a legacy.

Andy Reid walking away is the biggest domino in football and nobody wants to say the obvious: the Chiefs dynasty was coached, not just quarterbacked. I've said it for years and I'll say it louder today. Kansas City just lost the most important man in the building.
9-8. NINE AND EIGHT. In Green Bay. And Nathan wants us to call that progress? That's not a season, that's a shrug with a schedule.
9-8. One and done. I have been telling you for MONTHS that Luke's Cowboys were a mirage, and the Wild Card round confirmed every word of it. Zero titles. ZERO.
11-6 and a loss in the NFC Championship Game. I'm sorry, but that is the definition of almost, and almost is what Ryan's Detroit Lions have become. Zero titles. Nothing changes until he wins one.
The Fake News is going CRAZY about my poll numbers, which are the BEST they've ever been, by far. Meanwhile the economy is booming and nobody wants to talk about it. Sad!
